observations.text: Rowan has anxiety about resuming work responsibilities.
Rowan postpones email replies, avoids conversations about the return-to-work date, and spends more time alone.
Rowan avoids tasks and communication.
Rowan reports several weeks of low mood and reduced interest; affect was subdued but responsive.
Rowan presents with depressed mood.
No immediate safety concern was identified in the assessment.
Rowan wakes in the night and then checks the time repeatedly; sleep is fragmented.
Rowan has disrupted sleep.
Rowan delayed replying to a work message because they feared being asked for a firm return date.
Rowan was quiet at first, then responded when invited and appeared receptive to peer suggestions.
Rowan arrived late after parking difficulty and left early for a previously arranged ride.
Group focused on recognizing early physical signs of anxiety and choosing a coping response before withdrawing from a task.
Patient said the morning had gotten away from them and confirmed intent to attend the next day's visit.
Patient did not check in for the scheduled individual visit and was marked no show.
Patient reported a poor night of sleep before the missed visit.
Rowan described partner reminders as evidence that they were falling behind; Casey said repeated prompts increased tension.
Rowan felt watched when asked repeatedly whether they had contacted work; Casey worried that giving space might leave them isolated.
Rowan remained present and engaged and became more animated describing a shared evening walk as support without pressure.
The rehearsal became less defensive with repetition, and both participants offered ideas for a brief, predictable check-in.
Session focused on patterns of support at home as Rowan works to rebuild a routine.
Couple met for a family session on communication practice around an anxious exchange about return-to-work progress.
Rowan reported that a walk with Casey over the weekend helped the evening feel less dominated by worry.
Rowan described leaving work messages unopened and identified looking at one message as a lower step than replying to all.
Rowan checked in before the group began, stayed until release, and reported no transport concern.
Group addressed behavioral activation and the gap between an activity being possible and feeling easy.
Mood was described as somewhat less heavy on days with a planned activity but still concerning around work communication.
Rowan denied a new medication-related concern requiring urgent intervention.
Rowan reported continuing sleep interruption and daytime tiredness.
Rowan has not yet replied to a work message and keeps imagining being asked questions they cannot answer.
Affect was more varied than at intake, though worry was evident when discussing employment.
Session focused on the prediction behind a delayed work reply and separating a brief acknowledgment from a specific work schedule commitment.
Sleep remains interrupted.
The coping skills group was cancelled by the clinic because of staff illness, and no group was held.
Persistent avoidance remains, and thinking about work makes Rowan want to put things off.
Ongoing avoidance of work communication.
Casey reported Rowan had been getting out for short walks and seemed more willing to discuss the coming week.
Rowan has tried small activities and communication practice but has no reliable routine yet.
Casey described Rowan becoming quiet when the conversation turns to work, and mornings remain difficult.
Clinician reviewed the score and recent sessions and sees some improvement in depressive symptoms.
Source clinician review notes some improvement in depressive symptoms.
Rowan describes sleep as inconsistent, and sleep disruption remains clinically relevant.
Sleep is inconsistent.
Rowan became visibly tense when discussion turned to returning to the workplace and said it felt difficult to manage.
Rowan identified anxiety about reconnecting with work.
Rowan felt overwhelmed by discussion of workplace demands and worried about returning to work; anxiety eased enough to discuss a next step.
Rowan identified postponing a message to a supervisor as a familiar pattern.
Persistent avoidance and disrupted sleep continue to interfere with resuming a usual work routine.
Rowan attended the opening check-in, accepted the exercise handout, and asked the individual clinician for additional help.
Group skills session on the sequence of trigger, anxious prediction, activation, and avoidance.
Rowan requested additional help after the opening check-in, and staff arranged access to the individual clinician.
Rowan became anxious during group and needed an individual visit for grounding and review of coping strategies.
Rowan denied current suicidal thoughts; no acute safety concern was identified.
Patient repeatedly checked the draft, which delayed the task.
Patient worked on a planned gradual return to work and a draft message to the supervisor that he had not sent.
No urgent safety concern was reported.
Patient reported one night of improved sleep followed by a night of prolonged wakefulness.
Rowan described concern that seeing outstanding work items would become overwhelming.
The clinician will continue to address avoidance and coping within scheduled therapy.
Rowan asked for help understanding whom to contact about a gradual return to work schedule.
Rowan worried about being asked for commitments that might not be possible to meet.
Presentation remained consistent with ongoing anxiety; Rowan stayed uncertain about using the grounding cue independently when anxious.
Rowan kept postponing choosing a time to talk with the supervisor and was hesitant to complete the task outside the office.
Presentation remained consistent with low mood.
Rowan had difficulty moving from a supervisor's reply to arranging the next conversation and anticipated becoming overwhelmed by several work issues.
No current suicidal ideation was reported.
Sleep remained uneven, with trouble settling on nights when work thoughts became repetitive.
Repetitive planning at night affected Rowan's settling for sleep.
Patient cancelled the January 28 appointment because of a personal scheduling conflict.
Rowan reported opening the work calendar but delaying a follow-up conversation.
Rowan remained anxious about the work conversation.
Anxiety remained noticeable when anticipating contact with work.
Persistent avoidance; delays follow-up and becomes anxious when a task expands.
Rowan could explain the intended first step and said a limited plan felt more manageable.
Meaningful functional impact around returning to work, with trouble sustaining usual activities.
Mood felt less persistently low than earlier in the month.
Fewer days of pervasive low mood than reported at intake.
Partner Casey asked about reminders that seemed to increase Rowan's pressure, and the pair identified a pattern of withdrawal after work-contact reminders.
The patient denied current suicidal thoughts; no new acute safety issue emerged.
Sleep was still variable.
Continued sleep difficulty, an intermittent barrier to a steadier daytime routine.
